purpose: The depth audit David ruled on 2026-09-09 ("start reading our own 543 records against their sources on a schedule") and made this project's interim yardstick on 2026-09-10 ("judge the project meanwhile on how much of our own material stands up when we check it").

verdicts.SOUND: the cited source was read and it supports the row
verdicts.DEFECTIVE: the cited source was read and it does NOT support the row
verdicts.UNRESOLVED: the source was reached but could not settle the question (a truncated section, an abstract that cannot prove absence). NOT a defect and NOT a pass.
verdicts.UNREACHABLE: the source could not be read at all (paywall, 403, dead link)

meta.denominatorProvenance: COMPUTED, not remembered, since 2026-09-11: `node scripts/depth-audit.mjs --corpus` prints the partition with its definition and its control. It reads 770 bound rows across 115 constant files, 673 cited and 97 uncited. This REPLACES the 543-of-763 figures recorded on 2026-09-09 by a script that was never committed; see corpus.supersedes2026_09_09.
meta.samplingRule: NOT random, and the read must say so — but no longer chosen for suspicion either. SLICE 1 (A-47-0001..0003, 2026-09-10) was a deliberate hunt for discrepancy: two rows from 10a whose stated values differed from the figures in their cited papers TITLES, plus one row from 87a the mirror itself flags as bibliographically unverified. A sample selected for suspicion cannot be projected onto the corpus as a rate. SLICE 2 (A-47-0004..0008, 2026-09-11) is a SYSTEMATIC sample, deterministic and re-derivable without a seed: enumerate the cited bound rows in file-then-line order (the enumeration `node scripts/depth-audit.mjs --corpus` counts, 673 rows) and take positions 50, 150, 250, 350 and 450. It is still not a random sample and five rows settle nothing on their own, but unlike slice 1 it was drawn without looking at the rows first, so as slices accumulate at fixed positions the audited set stops being biased toward rows we already suspected. SLICE 3 (A-47-0009..0013, 2026-09-12) continues the same systematic ladder and was likewise drawn before any row was read: positions 550 and 650 complete the +100 ladder slice 2 began, and 100, 200 and 300 continue it offset by 50. The draw is no longer prose: `node scripts/depth-audit.mjs --draw 100 200 300 550 650` prints the rows at those positions from the same parser and the same cited-row definition the denominator counts, and each stored row carries the hash that draw printed. WHAT THE STORED HASHES DO AND DO NOT ESTABLISH (recorded 2026-09-12 at the adversarial review's insistence): each row carries the hash the draw printed, which proves the verdict belongs to the row that was drawn — selection IDENTITY. It does NOT prove the draw happened BEFORE the reading; nothing in the artifact orders those two events, and the claim that positions were fixed first rests on this session's own account. A timestamped draw receipt pinned to the mirror revision would make it independently checkable, and is not built.

corpus.definition: A BOUND ROW is a data row of the table under "## Known upper bounds" or "## Known lower bounds", HTML comments stripped and the table header and separator rows excluded — the repo own definition, lifted from extract-pins.mjs so the audit and the generated pins count the same things. A CITED row names at least one bracketed reference token anywhere in the row; that token is what a reader follows, and this same list is the audit sampling frame.
corpus.partitionControl: WHAT THE CHECKS PROVE, narrowed twice by adversarial review on 2026-09-11 because the first two statements of it overstated. The partition (673 cited + 97 uncited = 770 bound) proves only that the two classes EXHAUST the rows the parser enumerated; it cannot fail against real enumeration and is not evidence of completeness. Four narrow checks sit under it, each with a demonstrated failing case: the file inventory is checked against the mirror manifest own fileCount (round 2 showed a corpus of one intact file passing without it); every constant file must contribute at least one bound row; every section the committed generated pins expect must produce rows, which catches WHOLE-SECTION disappearance and nothing finer (round 2 drove 770/673 to 428/392 by renaming lower-bound headings while every file still contributed rows); and no line inside any bounds table BLOCK may fail to start with a pipe, which catches row loss within a section — every block in a section is walked, each block own header and separator excluded, and a blank line, blockquote, heading, HTML block or prose ends a block legally rather than being read as a lost row (round 3 stripped the optional leading pipe from 535 interior rows — legal GFM — and drove the corpus to 235/205 with every section still yielding its last row, so the pins and the section baseline both passed). A row that is well-formed, present, and simply absent from upstream is invisible to all of them, as it should be.
corpus.corpusControl: The 87a.md control A-47.note2 recorded reads 7 bound rows, 6 cited, carrying the string 857.5662 — identical under both the 2026-09-09 enumeration and this one. THAT IS THE WARNING, not the reassurance: the control passed under both while the totals differed by 130 rows, so a control that only asks whether a field is present cannot protect a number. It is pinned to its exact counts for that reason.
corpus.supersedes2026_09_09: The figures here REPLACE 543 cited of 763 bound rows with 220 uncited, recorded 2026-09-09. CORRECTED 2026-09-11 after adversarial review round 2 flagged this very sentence: the old denominator was NOT on all 115 pages. The audit block renders only on pages carrying an audited row, so at the previous commit it appeared on exactly one public page, c/10a.html (verified with git grep over HEAD; the other hits for that digit string are the value 0.5433 in Landau's constant, not a denominator). Those could not be reproduced. The mirror has not changed since 2026-09-07 (git log over ledger/teorth-optimizationproblems/constants prints nothing since then), so this is not drift, and three predicates were tried against the unchanged corpus: reference token anywhere in the row gives 673 of 770, reference COLUMN names a reference gives 656, column is exactly a bracketed token gives 461. None returns 543, and the 09-09 measuring script was never committed, so its definition is unrecoverable. WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE PUBLISHED FIGURE: the denominator was understated, which makes any coverage fraction read better than it is, and a number on our own public page could not be re-derived by the people we ask to re-derive everything else. The 87a control passed under both enumerations while the totals differed by 130 rows, which is why a control that only asks "is the field present" cannot protect a number.
corpus.staleWhen: These are a snapshot of the mirror as committed. Upstream adds and removes rows, so re-run the readCommand rather than quoting this block; the figure on the public page is only as fresh as the last render.
corpus.baselineIndependence: RECORDED BECAUSE IT LIMITS THE SECTION CHECK: the per-section baseline is read from the generated pins in ledger/claims.json, which extract-pins.mjs cuts with the SAME section-matching code this counter uses. It therefore detects a section that stops parsing relative to the last committed snapshot; it is NOT an independent parser, and it would not notice a definition both programs share being wrong in the same way. That is why the table-syntax check exists beside it rather than inside it.
corpus.guardHistory: FOUR ROUNDS OF ADVERSARIAL REVIEW SHIPPED SEVEN FIXES INTO THIS DENOMINATOR AND ITS GUARDS ON ONE DAY, and three of the seven were defects in checks I had just written to fix the previous one. The pattern is worth more than any single fix: a completeness guard over a format I do not control is a parser, and a hand-rolled parser fails quietly in exactly the direction that flatters the number. What survives is narrow and stated: each check names the one failure it catches, the section baseline is explicitly NOT independent of the pins it reads, and the partition is described as exhausting the enumerated rows rather than proving completeness.

reviewRounds.findings: MEDIUM: rows moved into a SECOND table block in the same section still vanished silently (235 bound / 147 cited at exit 0) because the anomaly scan stopped at the first blank line and never resumed. MEDIUM, and the more dangerous one: a blockquote or an ATX heading placed directly after a table legally ends it under GFM, and the scan read those lines as dropped rows and REFUSED an intact corpus — an ordinary upstream annotation would have disabled the denominator indefinitely, which is the permanently-red alarm this lane was founded on. Both fixed by replacing the hand-rolled scan with real block recognition: a block is a header followed by a separator row, every block in the section is walked with its own header and separator excluded, and a blank line, blockquote, heading, HTML block or prose ends it. The live corpus reads 770/673 before and after the rewrite, so the definition did not move. Both families are now selftest cases, the loss firing and the legal terminators staying silent with the counts proven intact. audits.rowText: | $< \dfrac{\pi}{2\ln(1+\sqrt{2})} - 10^{-4}$ | [SLXCKKM26] | Same team; via the first *asymptotic* Krivine-type rounding scheme (previous works only considered low-dimensional schemes). |

audits.evidence: The abstract states the bound verbatim: "We establish new bounds on the Grothendieck constant $K_G$: \[ \frac{6\pi}{11} \le K_G \le \frac{\pi}{2\log(1+\sqrt2)} - 10^{-4}. \]" The mirror row attributes exactly $-10^{-4}$ to this reference. Match.

audits.notes: DOWNGRADED FROM SOUND 2026-09-11 BY ADVERSARIAL REVIEW ROUND 2, on this row's own recorded evidence rather than a re-fetch. The mirror row states a STRICT inequality (its value cell opens with "<"), while the passage recorded here states a NON-STRICT one: the abstract gives the chain with "\le" at this threshold. A source proving "at most X" does not establish "less than X", so the cited passage does not support the row AS WRITTEN. UNRESOLVED, not DEFECTIVE: the paper may well establish strictness elsewhere, and nothing here shows the row is false. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: read the body for a strict statement at this exact threshold. RECORDED, NOT FILED — the row belongs to upstream, and any correction sent there is outward contact needing an adversarial review plus David's explicit gate (AGENTS.md outward gate).

audits.positiveControl: The body fetch returned the token 6.039, which the ABSTRACT does not contain — a wrong or truncated document could not have produced it. Title also confirmed.
audits.notes: THE METHOD FINDING OF THIS SLICE, worth more than the verdict. The paper is TITLED "... - 10^{-5}" and its ABSTRACT claims only $10^{-5}$. Read from the abstract alone this row looks WRONG, and I would have filed a defect against upstream for a bound the paper proves in its own Theorem 1.1. The title is the paper rounding its own sharper result. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE AUDIT: an abstract can never settle a value-vs-source row NEGATIVELY, only positively. A row whose abstract disagrees is UNRESOLVED until the body is read — never DEFECTIVE. This is the lane's standing HTTP-200 rule arriving through a new door: the document was genuine, complete and on-topic, and still could not answer the question asked of it. audits.fetchedAt: 2026-09-11, between 15:05Z and 15:20Z, in the session that recorded them
audits.evidence: DOWNGRADED FROM SOUND BY ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, 2026-09-11, before this ever shipped. What the abstract does settle: "We prove that for any log-concave random vector X in R^n with mean zero and identity covariance, E(|X| - sqrt(n))^2 <= C where C > 0 is a universal constant", and "This confirms the thin-shell conjecture in high dimensional convex geometry" — so the row resolution claim is supported. What it CANNOT settle, and why the verdict is UNRESOLVED rather than SOUND: (1) the row value cell parenthesises an equivalent variance form that this source states nowhere I read, and the equivalence is standard but unread here; (2) the row says the universal constant is "not optimized (and is not made explicit)", which is a claim about the PAPER, and an abstract that merely omits a value cannot establish that the body never supplies one. That is this lane own rule — an abstract can settle a value-versus-source row positively but never negatively (A-47-0002) — applied to a clause I had let through. Settling this row needs the body.
audits.positiveControl: The same fetch returned the title "Thin-shell bounds via parallel coupling", both authors (Klartag, Lehec), and the method tokens "Eldan's stochastic localization" and "Bourgain's slicing conjecture" — specific to this paper, so the artifact is the right one. audits.evidence: BOTH HALVES OF THE ROW ARE NOW SETTLED.
